title: A Simple Way To Keep Track Of Consequences https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2016/02/27/a-simple-way-to-keep-track-of-consequences/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin shares a low-tech documentation system for tracking student consequences, prompted by frequent reader requests on the topic. He recommends a printed monthly roster with one small square per student per day, marked with a simple check, dot, or line whenever misbehavior occurs, kept on a clipboard rather than a phone or laptop to avoid appearing distracted. For more serious incidents — a time-out or parent contact — teachers should jot a brief written description on an accompanying sheet, with an example log entry format included. He argues the low-tech, handwritten nature of the system makes documentation feel more credible to parents and administrators than digital records, and that having reliable records on hand reduces confrontations and skepticism during parent conferences, ultimately supporting the broader SCM philosophy of shifting responsibility for behavior onto students.

There are many options for documenting misbehavior, but I’ve found that a simple class roster and a clipboard to be a good way to go.
A clipboard is also easily accessible and won’t make you appear to be texting or checking your email during class.
Simple checks, dots, or vertical lines to represent each incident of misbehavior will do.

When you conference with parents, you can show them your documentation as a means of expressing concern, opening dialogue, or explaining why their child earned the grade(s) they did.
It shows that you’re on the ball and that your opinions and observations are accurate and supported by eyewitness descriptions.
